title: 0362-no-train-yet-gain-towards-generic
universal_lens: The McByte framework unifies tracking-by-detection by introducing a conditional, mask-derived cost perturbation to the standard Hungarian assignment. It operates as a dual-cue system: geometric IoU provides the baseline affinity matrix, while segmentation overlap (mf) acts as a higher-order topological prior, activated exclusively during combinatorial ambiguities or isolation singularities in the detection graph.
gsi_mapping: In GSI's Bayesian inference stack, the regulated mask cue functions as a dynamic likelihood modifier. When standard kinematic priors yield high posterior entropy (ambiguity), the segmentation overlap mf^{i,j} is injected as an auxiliary evidence term, effectively re-weighting the observation model to resolve identity switches without requiring per-sequence hyperparameter tuning.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the ambiguity/isolation gating represents a state-transition trigger. The engine monitors the association matrix; upon detecting a degenerate matching condition (multiple valid assignments or zero matches), it instantiates a heavy topological solver (SAM+Cutie). This ensures computational resources are strictly allocated to resolving complex spatial occlusions on the pitch.

primitives.name: Mask Fraction Overlap Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: mc gates but never directly modifies cost (multiple masks can fit in one box with mc=1.0 — misleading).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: mf^{i,j}: dimensionless ratio of intersection area over detection bounding box area; mask(tracklet_i): pixel set of temporally propagated segmentation; bbox_j: pixel set of current detection.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes SAM-initialized and Cutie-propagated masks maintain strict identity consistency across frames and that pixel-wise intersections accurately reflect physical object overlaps.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when detector bounding boxes are excessively loose, causing the denominator |bbox_j| to artificially deflate the overlap fraction, or when severe motion blur degrades mask boundaries.

primitives.name: Conditional Cost Perturbation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Update rule: costs^{i,j} = costs^{i,j}_{IoU} - mf^{i,j} if all conditions hold, else costs^{i,j}_{IoU}.
primitives.latex: costs^{i,j} = \begin{cases} costs^{i,j}_{IoU} - mf^{i,j}, & \text{if conditions (1)-(4) satisfied} \\ costs^{i,j}_{IoU}, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: costs^{i,j}: dimensionless assignment cost; costs^{i,j}_{IoU}: baseline Intersection over Union cost; mf^{i,j}: mask fraction overlap (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the baseline IoU cost and the mask fraction operate on comparable scales such that direct subtraction meaningfully alters the optimal Hungarian matching.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the gating conditions are too permissive, causing the mask cue to override correct kinematic predictions in low-occlusion scenarios.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's conformal prediction adjustment, where a secondary non-conformity score is subtracted from the primary p-value only when the initial confidence interval exceeds a predefined width.
layer2.telemetry: MOTA improvement delta between ByteTrack baseline and McByte.

primitives.name: Ambiguity and Isolation Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: The mask is *not* used blindly — it is applied only in two regulated cases: **ambiguity** (IoU-based cost below matching threshold for more than one tracklet–detection pair in a row/column) and **isolation** (all IoU costs above threshold, so no match possible).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Threshold: dimensionless IoU cost boundary; Ambiguity: boolean state indicating multiple sub-threshold candidates; Isolation: boolean state indicating zero sub-threshold candidates.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that standard IoU metrics are sufficient to identify degenerate states in the assignment matrix before invoking heavier topological cues.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur in extreme camera jitter where predicted bounding boxes shift drastically, falsely triggering isolation gates even when visual continuity exists.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSE's event-triggered state machine, transitioning from a lightweight Kalman filter regime to a heavy vision-language disambiguation regime based purely on matrix degeneracy.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of gate activations per minute of broadcast footage.

reasoning_traces.think:
The McByte operator fundamentally addresses the combinatorial explosion inherent in sports multi-object tracking (MOT) by decoupling the continuous kinematic state from discrete topological identities. Standard tracking-by-detection relies on a linear Gaussian assumption (Kalman filtering) paired with a greedy geometric association (IoU/Hungarian algorithm). This fails catastrophically during high-density occlusions (e.g., goal-line stands) where the IoU cost matrix becomes degenerate—yielding either multiple equally valid permutations (ambiguity) or no valid matches (isolation). Stanczyk et al. introduce a dual-layer cost function. The base layer remains the computationally cheap IoU distance. The secondary layer introduces a mask-fraction overlap (mf^{i,j}), derived from a foundation segmentation model (SAM) and temporally propagated via a video object segmentation network (Cutie). Crucially, this heavy topological prior is not applied globally. Instead, it is gated by a rigorous logical predicate evaluating the degeneracy of the IoU matrix. Mathematically, this creates a piecewise smooth optimization landscape. When the gradient of the IoU cost is flat (ambiguity) or undefined (isolation), the mf term injects a steep, discriminative gradient derived from pixel-level semantic consistency. The duality lies in trading compute density for combinatorial certainty: the system accepts a massive latency penalty (3-5 FPS) solely at the moments of highest epistemic uncertainty. The failure mode emerges if the underlying segmentation backbone loses identity consistency faster than the Kalman predictor diverges, causing the mf term to reinforce incorrect associations rather than correct them.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to the StrongSORT paradigm, which first integrated Re-ID embeddings into SORT's Kalman-Hungarian loop. However, McByte shifts the retrocausal anchor from a learned deep embedding space to a zero-shot, promptable segmentation manifold (SAM). Historically, MOT evolved from pure color histograms (Condensation) to rigid affine shapes (MCPHF), then to CNN features. McByte represents the convergence of foundational vision models with classical control theory, treating segmentation masks not as end-to-end outputs, but as auxiliary observables injected into a legacy tracking-by-detection kernel.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a game-theoretic perspective, the tracking engine acts as an observer attempting to decode the intentions of opposing agents who actively seek to induce occlusion (e.g., offensive linemen blocking receivers). The ambiguity gate mathematically formalizes the moment an agent successfully hides their trajectory from the geometric observer. By invoking the mask cue, the system attempts to 'see through' the intentional obstruction by relying on persistent texture and shape priors rather than fleeting centroid positions. The tracker essentially models the blocker's intent to maximize IoU collisions, and counters it by escalating to a higher-dimensional topological verification.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical anti-collinearity veto must be enforced: the mask cue must never override a highly confident kinematic prediction in open space. If the IoU cost is uniquely minimal and well below the threshold, the system must veto the segmentation update to prevent drift caused by segmentation artifacts (e.g., flickering masks due to motion blur). Furthermore, leakage vetoes are required if the SAM initialization inadvertently captures background elements (e.g., advertising boards) that share color profiles with player jerseys. The fixed thresholds (0.6/0.9/0.05) act as hard constraints to prevent the topological layer from dominating the geometric layer outside of true singularities.
